scope: Source review and prepared sparse-address experiment only; runtime execution pending
allocationPath: SharedMemory::new constructs MmapMemory and passes no initial memory image to LocalMemory::new.
MmapMemory reserves anonymous address space; the reviewed Linux implementation uses MAP_PRIVATE and MAP_NORESERVE.
Accessible initial pages and growth inside the reservation use mprotect rather than a bulk clear or copy.
The helper explicitly reserves 8 GiB of virtual address space, and the module imports that memory without data segments.
The sparse profile makes 4 GiB plus 128 KiB accessible and touches one 8-byte cell at address 4294967296 and one 4-byte wait cell at offset 8.
One-page growth is permitted exactly once. No dense fill, stress allocation, or guard-limit challenge is performed.

bounds.hugePages: disabled per process and checked before sparse mapping

claimLimit: This can establish sparse pointer-width, cross-isolate memory identity, callback and wait/notify correctness. It cannot establish dense allocation capacity, full Lean integration, other platforms or complete API behavior.
